title: Marketing lessons from Jake Paul: brand, audience appreciation and sponsorships
summary: Ross Jenkins uses Jake Paul as a case study for businesses. Key takeaways: appreciate your customers, build a recognizable brand, set high targets, believe in your offer, and use sponsorships (financial or in-kind) to borrow an influencer's audience. It is a high-level listicle with little concrete data.

principles.text: Appreciate your customers and give them news first; your business exists because of them.
principles.quote: Always appreciate them; show your clients that you’ve made it so far in business because of them.

principles.text: Build a personal or business brand boldly; being noticed drives growth and sales.
principles.quote: Don’t be afraid to build up your name. It helps a lot in growth and sales.

principles.text: Differentiate by doing business differently and finding new ways to market your brand.
principles.quote: He built his brand by doing business differently, embracing the controversies that make him more famous.

principles.text: Set high targets and believe your offer is the best in the market.
principles.quote: You have to believe that whatever you are offering is the best in the market at that current time.

principles.text: Sponsorships (financial or in-kind) let brands borrow an influencer's audience for awareness and credibility.
principles.quote: by using the large following of a social-media influencer like him, they can increase their brand awareness and credibility.

principles.text: Choosing the right sponsors for your content improves your odds of online success.
principles.quote: finding the right sponsors for your content can increase your chances for success.
